record.paper_title: Regularity of maximal operators: recent progress and some open problems
record.original_question: For 0 < beta < 1, let M_beta be the one-dimensional centered fractional maximal operator M_beta f(x) = sup_{r>0} |B(x,r)|^{beta-1} integral_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy, and let q = 1/(1-beta). Is the derivative map f -> (M_beta f)' both bounded and continuous from W^{1,1}(R) to L^q(R)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a parameter $\beta\in(0,1)$ and set $q=\dfrac{1}{1-\beta}$. For a locally integrable function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, define the one-dimensional centered fractional Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator by
$$M_\beta f(x)=\sup_{r>0}\,|B(x,r)|^{\beta-1}\int_{B(x,r)}|f(y)|\,dy,\qquad x\in\mathbb{R},$$
where $B(x,r)=(x-r,x+r)$ and $|B(x,r)|=2r$. Let $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R})$ denote the Sobolev space of integrable functions whose distributional derivative is also integrable, equipped with the norm $\|f\|_{W^{1,1}}=\|f\|_{L^1}+\|f'\|_{L^1}$.

It is known that for $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R})$ the function $M_\beta f$ is weakly differentiable. Decide whether the map
$$f\;\longmapsto\;(M_\beta f)'$$
is (i) bounded and (ii) continuous as a map from $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^q(\mathbb{R})$.
artifact.status_search_result: Boundedness of f ↦ (M_β f)' from W^{1,1}(ℝ) to L^q(ℝ) follows from earlier work of Kinnunen–Saksman. The continuity part was established by Beltran, Madrid and collaborators in "Continuity of the gradient of the fractional maximal operator on W^{1,1}(ℝ^d)" (arXiv:2102.10206), which proves continuity of f ↦ |∇M_α f| from W^{1,1}(ℝ^d) to L^q(ℝ^d) for all α∈(0,1) and all dimensions d≥1, covering the one-dimensional centered case in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Continuity of the gradient of the fractional maximal operator on W^{1,1}(R^d)
status_evidence.snippet: The map f ↦ |∇M_α f| is continuous from W^{1,1}(R^d) to L^q(R^d), where α∈(0,d), q=d/(d−α), for both the centered and non-centered fractional maximal operators; covers d≥1 and α∈(0,1) in full generality.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes continuity of the gradient of the centered fractional maximal operator from W^{1,1} to L^q in all dimensions, including d=1.
